title: SR2021 No7 2026 anaerobic-digestion waste-recovery emissions QA controls

sources.title: SR2021 No 7: anaerobic digestion facility, including use of the resultant biogas – waste recovery operation

facts.source_fact: SR2021 No7 is a waste recovery operation with treatment capacity not exceeding 100 tonnes per day and no more than 35,000 tonnes accepted per year.
The standard rules apply to England.
The rules were updated on 26 February 2026.
Use of the standard rules permit depends on meeting the rules and managing the generic risk assessment.
The published history confirms the annual acceptance cap is 35,000 tonnes, correcting an earlier 100,000-tonne error.
The 2026 update changed Activity 4 for biogas and biomethane treatment.
The 2026 update added captured, treated and stored carbon dioxide conditions.
The generic risk assessment was updated to include accidental carbon dioxide release.
CCR/HCR claims require a site-specific decarbonisation readiness report.
The readiness report must be reviewed at intervals not exceeding 2 years.
Point-source emissions are prohibited except from listed sources and emission points.
Point-source emission locations must be shown on a site plan.
Biogas combustion stacks require annual periodic monitoring over at least one hour.
MCERTS certification or accreditation is required where available for the monitoring programme unless otherwise agreed.
The listed NOx limit for biogas combustion plant is 500 mg/m3 using EN 14792.
The listed carbon monoxide limit is 1400 mg/m3 using EN 15058.
The listed total VOC limit including methane is 1000 mg/m3 using EN 12619.
Methane leak detection, programmed maintenance inspections and repair must be carried out and recorded.

Biogas upgrading to produce carbon dioxide is limited to specified physical treatment methods such as membrane separation, adsorption, scrubbing, distillation, compression, condensation, drying or cooling.
Separated carbon dioxide produced under the rule must meet food and beverage or industrial grade standards for use.

guard_patterns.handling: Preserve the cited rule exactly in scope.
Attach waste-recovery classification, capacity and annual cap.
Carry method, frequency, standard and emission-point provenance.
Do not infer parcel emissions from permit controls.
